_what: SECTION-5 RESIDUE: verified migration-ledger rows whose ORIGINAL body stays reachable from host code ON PURPOSE, so report_promotion_reconciliation.py section 5 stops counting them as findings and the FULL --check can be a lint gate.
_why_this_file_exists: Section 5 answers 'can original code still enter a body we own', and until SIM1-H every row it
named was open work -- which is why the lint gate was the narrow --check-flags and the wide
--check was 'supposed to be red'. SIM1-H drains the last 24 by translating and promoting their
eight reaching callers. What is left is not open work: it is four rows whose original staying
reachable is the DECIDED end state. A decided end state with no written adjudication reads
exactly like undrained work, so it gets written down here and the wide gate turns on.
THE RATCHET, and it is what makes an entry a claim rather than an exemption. Each row records
the FULL set of callers the section-5 closure reaches it through, computed with the cut nodes
excluded. The whole argument for the register-hazard rows is 'every edge forcing this is
front-end code the revised M6 exit (docs/reimpl-plan.md Sect. 5) leaves in the binary' -- so a
caller appearing that this adjudication never saw is precisely the event that must re-open it.
report_promotion_reconciliation.py re-derives the set on every run and FAILS BY NAME on a
drift, on an undispositioned row, and on a disposition whose row has left section 5 (stale).
Same refusal shape as reconciliation_pruned_roots.json's --check-roots and
undef_call_dispositions.json's refutes_if.
IT IS NOT A PLACE TO PARK WORK. Adding a row here is asserting that installing the redirect
would be WRONG, not merely unfinished. Three of the original four were the REBIND-AI-ESI
hazard class (docs/dead-ends.md): an entry redirect serves EVERY original caller, including
register state the committed prototype does not cover, so installing one was a live risk
rather than a chore. THOSE THREE ARE GONE, and how they left is the point -- not by the risk
being re-judged, but by the RE being done: the missing register contract was named and
committed, which turned the objection into a thunk. That is the only way a register_hazard row
may be removed. One row remains, and it is a different class entirely.
_measured: 2026-09-11 (LIB-REF-IN), at EN v402. The THREE register_hazard rows LEFT this file: their register contracts were named and committed (flash/select __mh_watcall_ebx_volatile, planet_distance __mh_watcall_ecx_ebx_volatile), so the generated thunk now marshals what used to be ambient EBX/ECX and the REBIND-AI-ESI objection no longer applies -- they are ordinary sim_hostreach installs (18 -> 21). Previously: 2026-09-10 (SIM1-H), at EN v400, section 5 went 28 -> 4 when the eight SIM1-H callers were promoted.

dispositions.name: llm_map_fog_of_war_recompute
dispositions.why: reached only through map_LoadPlanetFromDisk, itself a NAMED RESIDUE (the save closure is ours in no configuration)
detail: map_LoadPlanetFromDisk is promotable and deliberately NOT promoted at ship -- it is in this
tool's own RESIDUE table with the reason (the original writes/reads the planet file; the
promotion is exercised by promote_save.ini in its own runs, SV1-P-LOAD). Because the
original load walker is what runs, its call into our fog-of-war body is a REAL original
edge, and it will stay one for exactly as long as mh::config::kSaveClosureOwned is false. This row is
therefore not independent: it expires when the save/load wave ships promoted, and until
then installing a redirect on it would be installing around a decision recorded elsewhere.
REFUTES_IF, beyond the caller-set ratchet: map_LoadPlanetFromDisk leaves the RESIDUE table
(i.e. kSaveClosureOwned becomes true). The mechanical arm covers it -- cutting that node drops
this row out of section 5 entirely, and the STALE check then fails asking for the row here
